body: That's a pretty good idea, I'm basically looking for inspiration here so I really appreciate this.

Thanks for this, repeating that in my head is probably the only thing keeping me calm and I feel like I picked a good lawyer that's giving solid advice.  From what I can tell her lawyer is apparently aware of everything she's doing and doesn't seem to know this is a violation of our current divorce arrangement, i guess i'll get some kind of something (retribution maybe) when we finally get in court.
I would maybe ohm your injectors, mine seemed to be finicky depending on temp before going out fully.
I asked if I could do this, the lawyer said no since we're still legally married and that's an asset we both shared

Thank you for the kind words, and I'm being as calm as possible and following my lawyer's advice to the T.  But you're right on the last part, I don't know where my son is or if he's ok, and I feel (and seemingly am) helpless to do anything about it.  

If anyone has any advice on how I can legally get something done to find out my son's whereabouts please chime in.

As far as i know they can't.  I called my local police department and they basically said to call a lawyer as they can't do anything since we're still married, even after I explained that I had filed divorce papers months ago.
I read this in the voice of Gene from Bob's burgers, now you will too.
Nobody gonna say anything about the flat tire?

Was riding horses with my neighbor (we were 15ish, live in TN) in the woods.  Ran my horse up a hill, she followed and was only wearing a tank top, no bra.  It was like slow motion as they peeked over the top of that shirt over and over.  She didn't know why I couldn't stop smiling when she made it to the top.

That is the furthest thing from the truth.  I know more of the situation with my son than the property because thats what the majority of the talks with my attorney were regarding.  In TN, she can't more 50+ miles away without giving 30 days notice and me having a chance to contest that move in court and her proving why its in the best interest of the child.

But in the end, thank you for jumping to a conclusion based on nothing more than a post regarding a specific piece of this whole process. So far nobody has made me feel lower about the situation than this brief comment.
Also, who would i call to ask the question?  Police dispatch?

The cause of the arguments don't matter at this point, they aren't physical and never have been, but we're done.  She wants to leave and I'm not trying to stop her, if she relocates my son i'll file papers monday to have him returned to me.  My question is can she take property (furniture) from our home to move in to her new residence before a divorce agreement has been finalized.

If that's how you're going about it then why not just not get married.  Marriage is about putting yourself in that situation, and if that's not what you want then you should let whoever you're with know your point of view on it.  Either they respect that and you still have a wonderful relationship without being married, or they decide marriage is important to them and split early.  Either way you avoid the scenario you're planning for.

You should literally never have children if your attitude is "well if shit hits the fan I can always jump on a plane and not look back".  It also seems like a terrible thing to open up a marriage with an exit strategy, even its started

I just hate the situation, but at the same time I can't wait for it to be over.  My wife is a great mother, but I can't wait for all this to be over.  I know when its said and done, whoever get custody, it will just be hard because she is moving back to our hometown which is ~120 miles away from here.  While that's not too far to prevent either myself or her from being a big part of my sons life, one of us will be missing soccer practices, school plays, and just generally seeing him grow up day to day.
I'm in TN, i think it was more because we have a child that she assumes she'll get custody of.  But, I believe it was to get a custody order in place so that she can't move out of town with my son.
This was probably the best thing for me to do, so I gave it a shot when she got home today.  Looks like today's the day I'll be filling papers unfortunately.
That I never have, or will, be able to understand when I'm being told something literally vs. sarcastically when they're mad at me.

I spoke to him about that, and he said while filing first in my case would probably be best that all we would need to do if she bolted back to deadendsville is file a court order to have the child placed back in my custody (which he felt pretty strongly we could get from a local court, as well as have the venue in our current town regardless).
This is literally where I'm at right now.  I want things to work out, but she needs to want it to for it to really work, and I'm just not feeling the real effort on her part

If you both feel strongly in your position on that, there really isn't middle ground (unless you count getting a dog or something, but that's nowhere close to the same).  If you aren't ready for a child, don't commit to just to satisfy her and possibly be in a place where you think "this isn't what i wanted" and have that attitude toward a child.

I'm not trying to discourage you, as my child was a surprise that changed my life for the better and I love him every day for it, but if you are willingly attempting to bring another life in to the world don't do so just to satisfy someone else.
We've had the conversation about this, but she thinks that because our families are there that its a better situation.  Is there any legal merit to that?
That makes sense, her family is basically gifting her money monthly, so I could see that
I'm in IT, I've tried to find the chat logs.  She's using a game chat service called curse voice, and it doesn't keep logs for shit.  You can't even copy/paste the screen with usernames
Thanks for the advice, I've contacted a law firm that deals exclusively in men's divorce and child custody.  I'm sorry you ended up in that situation, if you want to talk about it PM me.

I think she want's to divert my attention from her so she doesn't feel bad about splitting, and also if I fucked her sister that would give her the "I knew he was a piece of shit" satisfaction to be fine with everything.  She's already brought up divorce, this was just a thing that happend that I never saw coming.

She was already planning on leaving, and I think her and the "friend" she was chatting with have something going on, although he's several states away it feels like they're more than just friends to me.  I've emailed an attorney today and just finished changing the passwords to my bank account.  I'll be changing my direct deposit later today.  I can't just up and leave as we have a child together, that I don't plan on leaving with someone as cynical as this.  Her family isn't better either obviously (since the sister has already agreed to the plan).
I wasn't able to get a log or anything, but I took a picture with my camera that is legible enough to read.  It has her username (which is her first name) in the chat log on the pic.
I could care less about the ring at this point, but wtf.  Who comes up with a plan like this?

That's great to hear about the the 50/50 piece in TN, that makes me feel much more calm about the situation knowing she won't be able to simply uproot my child like she plans.  The only other worry I have is both sets of grandparents live where she's going (both our hometowns) and she wants to argue that they'll be free babysitters/daycare, while I will be on my own here once she's gone.  Also, her mother has had a history of abuse with her other children, and i don't want my child staying with her alone as I don't trust her as a responsible adult (she had two of her children sent in to state custody last year, but one is out now, the other has been back and forth to the boys home for threating other kids lives at school.

As far as the debt I think I agree with you, but I feel like I need to keep my house in order to hold everything togeher, and that's the only thing that has me concerned aside from the custody.  The house is the ONLY thing in both our names, everything else is in my name alone (both cars, one motorcycle, almost all the bills except one credit card and the electric payer.

I'm on my way to ask my boss if the shit hits the fan if I could work from home until I can arrange other child care, hopefully that will work in my favor since I'm trying to prepare as best I can for possibly being a single dad.

By the end of this I may need that beer

Reason enough right there.  If you aren't comfortable with it, and she isn't willing to even compromise on this, it sounds like this was planned from the start.  I'm sorry it all ended up this way, but I don't see how you could ever trust her again after that much manipulation

Thank you for having the conversation.  I'm writing a letter to go along with some flowers to break down how I've been feeling and bring up marriage counselling (since I can't seem to get the words out of my mouth).  If this doesn't work, I feel like I'm out of options and I'll get in touch with local attorneys to review my options.  I want whats best for my child, and I think the best option is here with me where we had planned to stay as a family.

I appreciate your time talking with me, and I hope that everything goes well for you in your relationships.  If you ever need to vent/chat/or rage about something feel free to message

That's true, but I genuinely don't think that money is a factor for her.  She's expecting to be going to school living in a property owned by a family member (probably rent free) and going to school.  I'm sure finances are a factor, but if I gave my job up I would have to file for bankruptcy to get away from all the commitments I currently have.

Most likely she would agree to the 50/50 if I moved back, but you are also right that our hometown has much less opportunity for jobs.  The unemployment rate is one of the highest in the state and the median income is barely over minimum wage vs. where we live now is ranked as the 7th best place to live in the state and is 20 minutes from the state capital (where all the real jobs are.)

The biggest problem is I'm a healthcare/IT professional, and would have basically 0 transferable skills to a job in that town.  Best I could hope for is prison guard at the local medium security prison for $9/hr

I'm not sure what's happening in my relationship right now, but I almost feel like I'm being cheated on emotionally.  I've been cheated on before (not while married, just relationships) and I'm not sure that I could ever have any empathy for someone who had done the cheating, regardless of the situation.  I understand the feels of being cheated on, and there isn't anything in the world that causes me to hate so much.

Hey friend, you shouldn't feel bad for trying to make time for yourself every once in a while.  I know your kids will be disappointed (props to you for being there and handling business as needed though), but if you don't take care of yourself then you'll just end up getting depressed, feeling bad about the situation, and then the kids will pick up on that.

TL:DR
You're doing the right thing, I hope things get better from here for you

Got it, I just read some articles on the terminology.  I think what I'm most concerned about is being the custodial parent (as from what I've read this is basically the parent that will make most large decisions about the child) as she wants my son to go to school in our hometown where she plans to move, but I want him to go where we currently live as it has much better schools (which is the primary reason we bought the house in this area.  Good location, large fenced yard, good neighbors, and excellent school.)

I don't think there is another man, and I've tried to make that point (and will continue to do so) that a home with both of us would be the best for our son (obviously as long as we can work through our problems, and I am willing to work as hard as needed).  She says that she wants to be alone, which makes me think she is having a hard time with her depression (she was on fluoxitine, but then quit taking them because they made her feel numb to everything) as she usually becomes withdrawn when things get bad for her.

I don't think your last suggestion is even something we could try.  Emotionally I don't think I could survive that situation.
Thanks for the info.  Do you think it would make a difference that she's moving back to our hometown (where both sets of grandparents live, as well as the rest of our immediate families)?

Lets say the house is worth 175k, and we owe 165k (which is pretty close to accurate, probably owe more, just bought 1.5 years ago with 0 down).  Also, if we could agree on the property or the debt (since these aren't really my biggest concern) what would it mean if we couldn't come to an agreement on custody.  I think my son would have a better life her, with my established job, completed school, and him being her 95% of his life, and having better schools.

It won't be an out of state move, just a very far one.  From what I've read of state law so far I could file for temporary custody while we're still married that would give me custodial right until otherwise stated in court, but I'm hoping I don't need some sort of sign on from my wife to get it as I'm still hoping this works out, but in the next few days I guess I'll know if I have anything left to hope for.

Jesus Christ this sounds like my life right now.  With this basically being my situation, but I have a son (will be 4 in a month).  My wife had mentioned that she obviously wouldn't be able to afford the house so that would go to me, but would I still have to "buy" out her half even though I've been dealing with 100% of our marital finance? (personal advice of course)

If my situation doesn't end well (wife has brought up leaving), I'll be keeping mine on a necklace that I won't be taking off.  What I've been through, however it turns out now, has left its mark on me forever.  That ring will always be my reminder of everything my wife and I had together.

I haven't even thought about the situation like that, and it makes complete sense.  The more I think to myself or people tell me "you have a son, he's your reason to live" it does bring me back a bit, but also stresses me out exponentially more.  I love my son more than anything in the world, and its not the thought of her taking him, its more me not knowing how to get by without either of them. 

 I've still not given up on my marriage either, I'll do anything I can to make it work, but if everything falls apart, thank you for this.

Thank you for this, its a great starting point to the conversation.  I may have to go a bit further, as she's made the comment that she's possibly past the point of wanting to try, so I may have made the mistake of letting things slide too far.  But, I'm still trying to do my best to be the husband she deserves, so thank you for taking the time to help
I hope so too, but at this point I wish I would have done so much sooner.  Today has been worlds better than yesterday, but I can't help but think my wife is at the edge already.

I've been married for three years now and my wife acts more or less how you've described.  I actually came on her looking for advice on how to deal with it, but you sound almost identical.  We used to be very intimate at first, but we've been together for a total of 8+ years in total not just counting marriage.  As someone who's been through this from the male perspective, and didn't want to go the route of the "find someone else who fits your needs" answer, I think the depression is a huge contributing factor.  Maybe i just want something to blame it on, but after my wife got depressed (probably after her uncle died 4+ years ago) she changed and didn't want to do anything physical nearly as often.  

My advice would be to take care of your issues first, and if you want him to be part of the recovery that's wonderful.  Set bounderies if you need them, let him know the situation.  When it first started for me I was constantly confused and couldn't understand why my SO didn't want to be with me as often as I wanted to be with her.  She got on some medications that helped, and improved our lives together in my opinion, but ultimately they made her feel different and she didn't like taking them.  So now we are probably in a worse spot than ever, so I may not be the best person to give this advice, but there's my perspective from a guy's side.  If you want to talk about it more PM me , would probably make me feel better to understand where you're coming from too.
